notes: In 0.29.1, the Save window of Export, and an export that the assistant starts without a file name, suggest your project's name as the file name; 0.29.0 suggested the project's folder name, which has a short code added at its end. Projects that use zoom, Ken Burns, transitions, fades or many photos now export much faster and usually use less memory, and look the same: in our lab tests on one laptop, a zoom-heavy two-minute reel went from 38 minutes to about 2 on a fast setup and from over an hour to under 3 minutes on a mid-range one; projects without those effects take about the same time. The Export dialog is simpler: the Resolution list never offers a size larger than your project, Frame rate only offers lower rates, Frame rate, Quality and the Graphics chip setting are under Advanced settings, the dialog starts fresh each time you open it and shows no expected time or file size before you press Export, and keys you press in it stay in it. PCs where a graphics chip is found have a Graphics chip setting (Auto or Off) there, where it replaces the old Full quality / Fast choice. If your graphics chip passed ArtDaddy's test for the size of your video, ArtDaddy now uses it for every export unless you set it to Off; the test now covers 4K at 50 or 60 frames a second and 1440p at 31 to 60, and 8K still uses the processor; if the chip stops an export, ArtDaddy starts it again by itself on the processor. While an export runs, ArtDaddy shows a rough time left about five seconds after the first picture and improves it as it goes, says "Finishing" over the last tenth, and says "taking longer than expected" if the export slows down a lot; if an export turns out much slower than expected, a banner says so with the time left and what to lower, and you can keep going or cancel. A failed export says why in one plain sentence, with the technical text under Show details. The assistant's instructions for exports changed, in the app and for outside assistants connected over MCP: it is told to use your project's own size and frame rate and the standard quality unless you name a value, never to guess how long an export will take, never to cancel an export because it is slow, and to say plainly what happened when one fails. It is no longer given a guessed export time, is told how an export ended when ArtDaddy restarts it for you, and gets the plain sentence and failure code, without folder paths, when one fails. The assistant also waits for the words of a file that is not ready and is brought back once when they are; a picture the AI service refuses no longer locks your chat; and the sign-in screens say when the server is waking up. A bar along the bottom of the window now shows what goes on in the background (a chip showing what is being transcribed, and the credits you have left); a transcription that fails is shown there with its error and a Retry button, and the assistant can tell a file that waits for transcription from one that is being transcribed. On PCs that ArtDaddy already knows transcribe speech on the processor, it now downloads a smaller speech-to-text file, which was faster in our tests (PCs with a graphics chip, PCs that already have the full-size file, Arabic and any language the smaller file has not been checked for keep the full-size file); if the usual download place is down it tries a second one and checks the file itself, and a speech download that fails says why and offers Retry. The privacy policy, in the app and on the website, now names that second place, says when the full-size file is downloaded as well, and says that, while you are signed in, the app asks our service which of its features should be switched off, when it starts, before an export or a transcription, and about every ten minutes while its window is open, and that this request carries only your sign-in and the app's version, never your media, your projects or anything you type; it also says "light compression on your processor" instead of "a faster setting of your processor", and ArtDaddy sends no new kind of usage data. After the update your PC's earlier export times and memory figures are not used any more; nothing is deleted. The first start after the update can take up to 30 seconds. macOS: after the update you click Always Allow when ArtDaddy asks for your Mac login password.
